battle.title: Subnet Slice-n-Dice
battle.description: Prefix lengths, masks, private ranges and host counts under pressure.

questions.text: In the address 192.168.1.0/26, what does the /26 tell you?
options: There are 26 subnets in the network
The first 26 bits identify the network
The last 26 bits identify the network
questions.answer: The first 26 bits identify the network
questions.explanation: The prefix length is the number of leading bits that form the network part; here 32 - 26 = 6 bits remain for hosts. It is not a host or subnet count, and it counts from the left, not the right.

questions.text: Which of these is a private (RFC 1918) IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: The private block 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255 contains 172.20.5.9. 172.32.0.1 and 192.169.1.1 look similar but sit just outside the private ranges.

questions.text: An office VLAN needs room for 50 devices. Which prefix gives the smallest subnet that still fits them?
questions.explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits: 64 addresses, 62 usable after network and broadcast. /27 gives only 30 usable, too few, while /25 gives 126 and wastes space.

questions.text: How many usable hosts do these prefixes allow? What does the program print?
questions.explanation: Usable hosts = 2^(32 - prefix) - 2, because the network and broadcast addresses are reserved. /28 gives 16 - 2 = 14 and /30 gives 4 - 2 = 2. The 16 and 4 options forget the reservation.

questions.text: A host 192.168.10.77 uses a /26 mask. What network address does this program print?
questions.explanation: A /26 mask ends in 192 in the last octet, so 77 AND 192 = 64 (binary 01001101 AND 11000000). The /26 blocks start at 0, 64, 128 and 192, and 77 lies in the 64 block, not the 0 block.

coding.title: Find My Subnet
coding.description: Given an IPv4 address in CIDR notation a.b.c.d/p, print the network address (the address with all host bits set to 0) and the number of usable host addresses, which is 2^(32-p) - 2.
coding.inputDescription: A single line: an IPv4 address in CIDR notation, such as 192.168.10.77/26.
coding.outputDescription: Line 1: the network address in dotted decimal. Line 2: the number of usable hosts.
